Yes, absolutely. You can safeguard a Google Form for kids applying for a scholarship, and you should. Below is a clear, parent and school friendly way to do it, without overcomplicating things.

---

## 1. Collect the Minimum Information Needed
Only ask for what is truly necessary.

**Avoid collecting**
- Home address (full)
- Social Security numbers
- Medical details
- Exact birthdate (use age range instead)

**Safer alternatives**
- First name + last initial
- Parent or guardian email (instead of child’s)
- Age range (example: 10–12, 13–15, 16–18)
- School name only (no ID numbers)

---

## 2. Add a Parent or Guardian Consent Section (Very Important)
At the top of the form, include a required consent acknowledgment.

**Example wording**
> This scholarship application is intended to be completed with a parent or legal guardian. By submitting this form, the parent or guardian confirms consent for the child’s information to be reviewed solely for scholarship consideration.

Add a **required checkbox**:
- ☐ I am the parent or legal guardian and consent to this submission

---

## 3. Turn OFF Email Collection (Unless Needed)
In Google Forms:
- Settings → General
- Turn **OFF** “Collect email addresses”  
OR  
- Clearly label the email field as **Parent/Guardian Email**

This prevents accidental child email collection.

---

## 4. Restrict Access to Responses
Protect who can see the data.

**Best practices**
- Limit response access to 1–2 trusted adults
- Do not share the response spreadsheet publicly
- Use Google Drive permissions: Viewer or Editor only as needed

Optional but smart:
- Store responses in a **separate Drive folder** with restricted access

---

## 5. Disable Public Editing and File Uploads
Unless absolutely required:

- Do **not** allow file uploads (this can expose personal data)
- Do **not** allow respondents to edit responses after submitting
- Do **not** allow “Anyone with the link can edit”

---

## 6. Add a Privacy & Data Use Statement
Near the bottom of the form:

**Simple, clear language**
> Information submitted will be used only for scholarship evaluation and will not be shared, sold, or published. All data will be securely stored and deleted after the scholarship process concludes.

---

## 7. Set a Response Auto-Delete Timeline (Manual but Important)
Google Forms does not auto-delete, but you can:
- Set a calendar reminder to delete responses after winners are selected
- Clearly state how long data will be kept (example: 90 days)

---

## 8. Optional Extra Safeguards (Recommended)
If you want to go a step further:
- Require the form to be completed **by a parent**
- Use a short application plus a follow-up interview instead of long written answers
- Avoid photos or videos unless absolutely necessary

---

- Write parent-safe legal consent language
- Review your actual form questions for compliance
- Create a “kid-safe scholarship application” template
- Help you make a parent-only version of the form

Yes. Given your constraints (minors applying directly, file upload required, single-use applications, and a public landing page), this **needs to be set up carefully**, but it **can be done safely in Google** if you follow the process below exactly.

I am going to give you the **exact, step-by-step build sequence** so nothing is missed.

---

# SKÅL Hospitality  
## Post-Secondary Scholarship Application  
**Open:** March 2 – April 10  
**Committee Review:** April 13  
**Application Type:** Single submission, public access, reference upload required

---

## OVERVIEW OF THE STACK (WHAT YOU ARE BUILDING)

You will use **three Google tools together**:

1. **Google Form** → collects applications  
2. **Google Site (single page)** → landing page + info + link to form  
3. **QR Code** → points to the Google Site (not directly to the form)

This gives you:
- A buffer between the public and the form
- Better control and messaging
- Reduced spam and misuse

---

# STEP 1: CREATE A DEDICATED GOOGLE ACCOUNT OR FOLDER (IMPORTANT)

Before creating anything:

### Option A (Best Practice)
- Use a **Skål-owned Google account** (not personal)

### Option B (If using personal)
- Create a **new Drive folder**:
  - Name: `SKAL Scholarship Applications 2026`
  - Share access ONLY with:
    - Committee Chair
    - 1 backup admin
  - No public access

All files and responses live here.

---

# STEP 2: CREATE THE GOOGLE FORM (DO THIS FIRST)

### 1️⃣ Start the Form
- Google Forms → Blank Form  
- Title:
  **SKÅL Hospitality Post-Secondary Scholarship Application**

- Description:
  > This application is for post-secondary students pursuing education in hospitality or related fields. Applications are open March 2 through April 10. All submissions are final.

---

## STEP 3: FORM SETTINGS (CRITICAL SAFEGUARDS)

Click **⚙️ Settings**

### GENERAL TAB
- ❌ Collect email addresses → OFF  
- ❌ Limit to 1 response → OFF (since minors may not have Google accounts)
- ❌ Allow response editing → OFF
- ❌ Show link to submit another response → OFF

✅ This ensures **single submission per applicant session**.

---

### RESPONSES TAB
- ❌ Accept responses → ON (until April 10)
- Link responses to spreadsheet → YES  
  (store in your secure folder)

---

### PRESENTATION TAB
- Confirmation message:
  > Thank you for applying. Your application has been successfully submitted and will be reviewed by the scholarship committee.

---

# STEP 4: ADD A REQUIRED CONSENT & ELIGIBILITY SECTION

This protects you legally even without parent involvement.

### Section Title:
**Eligibility & Consent**

### Required Checkbox (must be checked)
> ☐ I confirm that I am applying for a post-secondary scholarship, that all information provided is accurate, and that I understand this application will be reviewed solely for scholarship consideration.

Add **short answer confirmation**:
> Type your full name to confirm

This creates **affirmative consent on record**.

---

# STEP 5: APPLICATION QUESTIONS (SAFE STRUCTURE)

### Personal Info (Keep Minimal)
- First Name
- Last Name
- Age Range (dropdown)
  - Under 16
  - 16–17
  - 18+

(Avoid birthdates.)

---

### Education Section
- Current School Name
- Graduation Year
- Intended or Current Post-Secondary Institution
- Intended Field of Study (short answer)

---

### Short Responses (Limit Length)
- Why are you pursuing a career in hospitality?  
  (Paragraph, limit ~250–300 words)
- How would this scholarship support your education?  
  (Paragraph)

---

# STEP 6: REFERENCE LETTER UPLOAD (SAFE FILE HANDLING)

### File Upload Question
- Question type: **File upload**
- Required: YES
- Allowed file types:
  - PDF
  - DOC / DOCX
- Maximum files: 1
- Max file size: 10MB

⚠️ Google will require the applicant to **sign in to upload**  
That is unavoidable and acceptable.

Rename the question clearly:
> Upload one reference letter (PDF or Word document only)

Files will automatically store in your secure Drive folder.

---

# STEP 7: ADD CAPTCHA / BOT PROTECTION

Google Forms does **not** have native CAPTCHA, so do this instead:

### Use Google Forms “Response validation”
Add a short question:

**Question:**  
> What is 3 + 4?

- Type: Short answer
- Response validation:
  - Number
  - Equal to
  - 7
- Required: YES

This stops automated bots.

---

# STEP 8: SET APPLICATION WINDOW (DATES)

### On March 2
- Turn **Accept responses ON**

### On April 10 (end of day)
- Turn **Accept responses OFF**
- Update confirmation message:
  > Applications are now closed. Thank you for your interest.

---

# STEP 9: CREATE A GOOGLE SITE LANDING PAGE

### Purpose
This page:
- Explains the scholarship
- Hosts the link to the form
- Is what your QR code points to

---

### Google Site Content Structure

**Header**
- SKÅL Hospitality
- Post-Secondary Scholarship Initiative

**Section 1: Overview**
- Purpose of scholarship
- Who should apply
- Key dates

**Section 2: Application Requirements**
- Online application
- One reference letter upload
- Short written responses

**Section 3: Important Notes**
- One submission per applicant
- Applications close April 10
- Incomplete submissions will not be reviewed

**Button**
> Apply Now  
(Link to the Google Form)

---

# STEP 10: QR CODE CREATION (DO NOT LINK DIRECTLY TO FORM)

- Generate QR code pointing to the **Google Site**
- Place on flyer
- Label clearly:
  > Scan to apply for the SKÅL Hospitality Scholarship

This gives you:
- Fewer accidental submissions
- A clear entry point
- Better optics for minors

---

# STEP 11: COMMITTEE REVIEW SETUP (APRIL 13)

Before April 13:
- Export responses to a **committee-only spreadsheet**
- Remove access to uploaded files for anyone not reviewing
- Optional:
  - Assign anonymized IDs
  - Hide last names if needed

---

# STEP 12: DATA RETENTION & CLEANUP

After decisions:
- Retain data only as long as necessary
- Delete files for non-recipients after review period
- Keep winner records only

---

✅ Public landing page  
✅ Single-submission form  
✅ Required consent  
✅ Reference upload secured  
✅ Bot protection  
✅ Controlled access  
✅ QR-friendly
